title: Integral pullback and completed tensor product preserve constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer
$\varpi_E$, $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of
schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ ($W\in\{X,Y\}$)
be the derived-complete integral constructible categories, and let $Lf^*$ and
$\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}$ be the integral derived pullback and
completed tensor product. Then:

1. for $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ one has $Lf^*K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$,
and for every $n$ the canonical map gives
$(Lf^*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong f^{-1}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$;
2. for $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ one has
$M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, and
$(M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong
(M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$
for every $n$.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9 (5) (pullback followed by completion preserves constructible complexes), Lemma 6.5.5 (D_cons is closed under tensor products), Lemma 6.5.3 (constructible complexes are bounded) and Lemma 6.5.4 (reductions)

proof.text: Write $B_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_Y}(A_{E,n})_Y$, and similarly $M_n,N_n$. Use the single K-flat resolutions with flat terms in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] their reductions remain K-flat with flat terms. For $m\geq n$, $(P\otimes_{B_W}A_{E,m})\otimes_{A_{E,m}}A_{E,n}=P\otimes_{B_W}A_{E,n}$, by the map $(p\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes ab$. Thus the reduction towers are normalized, with the quotient cocycle: both composites for three indices send the same pure tensor to its product.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion; explicit K-flat quotient calculation

proof.text: Put $U_n=f_n^*K_n$ and $V_n=M_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}N_n$. For $U_n$ use termwise pullback of the reduced resolution; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] makes it K-flat, For $m\geq n$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] and the canonical constant-ring identification of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] give $(f_m^*P_m)\otimes_{(A_{E,m})_X}(A_{E,n})_X\cong f_n^*(P_m\otimes_{(A_{E,m})_Y}(A_{E,n})_Y)=f_n^*P_n$. Indeed pullback commutes with tensor, its pullback of $(A_{E,n})_Y$ is $(A_{E,n})_X$, and step 1 identifies the quotient complex with $P_n$. These natural maps commute with quotient transitions because both composites multiply the same coefficient factors. For $V_n$ use $P_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}Q_n$ as in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. This total tensor is K-flat: tensoring an acyclic complex first with $Q_n$, then with $P_n$, remains acyclic. It has flat terms since tensoring by each term is a composite of exact tensor functors and the direct sums of flat terms are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct], applied in the Grothendieck abelian symmetric monoidal closed category of module sheaves. Scalar extension to $A_{E,n}$ of the level-$m$ total tensor identifies with $P_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}Q_n$, via $(p\otimes q)\otimes a\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(q\otimes a)$. The inverse multiplies the two coefficient factors. These degreewise maps commute with the total differential and quotient maps. Hence both $(U_n)$ and $(V_n)$ are normalized DVR towers in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], with coherent transition data coming from these strict complexes.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (5); termwise tensor and quotient calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to the two normalized towers. Their limits are precisely $Lf^*K$ and $M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N$ by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Both limits are derived complete, and the effectivity counits identify their reductions with $U_n$ and $V_n$ for every $n$. Since those counits are adjoint to the tower projections, these are the canonical maps of the assertion, not arbitrary isomorphisms. Finally [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] identifies $f_n^*K_n$ with $f^{-1}K_n$, with its transported finite-coefficient module action.

proof.text:
At a fixed level $n$, let $F$ be any constructible $(A_{E,n})_Y$-module sheaf. Choose the finite stratification $i_

u|$ has the same fibre as the immersion at $y$, since the immersion induces the same residue field there. They are pairwise disjoint and cover $X$. Their constructibility follows from [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage]. They are locally closed: preimages preserve open and closed subsets. The fibre-product scheme structures give immersions: write each $i_
u$ as a closed immersion into an open subscheme; its pulled-back open is an open subscheme of $X$, and on affine patches the pulled-back closed immersion is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)	o\operatorname{Spec}B$. These are precisely the open and closed immersion descriptions of [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text:
The site base-change construction in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] identifies $i^{\prime}_
u{}^{-1}f^{-1}F$ with $f_
u^{-1}i_
u^{-1}F$: both inverse-image composites are left adjoint to direct image along the same composite scheme morphism, whose direct images agree by associativity of fibre products. A covering $\{U_j	o Y_
u\}$ trivializing $i_
u^*F$ pulls back to a covering $\{X_
u	imes_{Y_
u}U_j	o X_
u\}$, since the site construction sends coverings to coverings. On the latter, the restriction is the same constant finite module $M_j$. Indeed a constant finite set sheaf is the coproduct of copies of the terminal sheaf indexed by its elements; inverse image, being a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint of a morphism of sites, preserves the terminal object and coproducts. It therefore preserves this constant sheaf, and also its addition and scalar-operation tables by finite-product preservation. The constant coefficient ring and module action agree with the transport specified in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Thus $f_n^*F$ is locally constant with finite module stalks on every $X_
u$, and is intrinsically constructible by [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Empty strata may be discarded; for empty $X$ retain a single empty stratum.

proof.text: Choose the single interval $[r,s]$ for all $K_n$ supplied by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Exactness of $f_n^*$ in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] identifies the pulled-back cycles, boundaries and their quotient: $\mathcal H^i(U_n)=f_n^*\mathcal H^i(K_n)$. Explicitly, cycles are kernels of differentials, boundaries are kernels of their cokernels, and exactness preserves these kernels, cokernels and quotients. The previous two steps show these cohomology sheaves are constructible. For $i\notin[r,s]$ they vanish because an additive functor sends zero to zero. Hence every $U_n$ belongs to the intrinsic finite-torsion category [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], with the same interval $[r,s]$. The completeness and canonical reduction identifications in step 3 now verify every condition of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] for $Lf^*K$.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(5), finite-reduction argument implemented using intrinsic constructibility and exact finite pullback

proof.text: Choose intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ for the cohomology of $M_1$ and $N_1$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], all $M_n$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and all $N_n$ have Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$, with the same bounds for every $n$. By [lem-sf-flat-model], choose bounded flat representatives $F_n,G_n$ in these intervals. Their total tensor represents $V_n$, and its degree-$j$ term is $\bigoplus_{u+v=j}F_n^u\otimes_{A_{E,n}}G_n^v$. It is zero unless $a+c\leq j\leq b+d$. Consequently the cohomology of every $V_n$ is contained in the single interval $[a+c,b+d]$. The flat representatives here serve only to prove the bound; the coherent tower remains the one constructed in step 2.

Each $M_n,N_n$ is bounded constructible by the definition of the integral category. Apply [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology] at level $n$: every cohomology sheaf of $V_n$ is constructible. Together with the bound in step 7 this says $V_n\in D^b_c(W,A_{E,n})$ for every $n$. Step 3 gives derived completeness of the limit and identifies these $V_n$ with its reductions. The single interval $[a+c,b+d]$ verifies the remaining uniform-amplitude requirement of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Thus $M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, with exactly the reduction isomorphisms already obtained in step 3.
